choices.text: Look again at what you already found.

nodes.text: He has been dead some hours. No wound you can see, no disarray beyond the chair pushed back. His right hand is still curled where the cup would have been.

The lips have gone the colour of a bruise, and there is a sediment in the cup's heel — dried, faintly furred. Foxglove. Steeped and strained badly by someone in a hurry. You would know it anywhere; so would anyone who sells tinctures for a living.

No wound, no bruising at the throat, nothing under the nails. Whatever took him was in him rather than done to him — you are sure of that much and no more. The cup holds a residue you cannot name, and naming it is exactly the thing that would have been useful.
Nothing has changed. He is still a man who drank something, and still not saying what.
You leave him the little dignity the angle of the chair allows.
